source.test: restoreBackup(_:) removeWorldFolders / unzip sequence, no rollback on failure

msc1_behavior.user_message: The backup ZIP could not be extracted. A safety backup of the previous world was created before the restore.
msc1_behavior.recovery_path: manual -- operator must find and restore the pre-restore safety backup by hand

phase6_correction.behavior: on a nonzero unzip exit, Phase 6 automatically restores the just-created pre-restore safety backup itself before returning the error, so a failed restore never leaves the server worldless

notes: This is a D-006-style correction, not oracle parity. MSC 1 removes the live world folders unconditionally (line 668, no temp-staging or atomic swap) before extracting; if /usr/bin/unzip then fails (line 672-684), the server has NO live world at all until someone manually finds and restores the pre-restore safety backup created two steps earlier (line 639). This is exactly the gap the P6.6 plan text calls out: 'failed/interrupted restore ... Where Phase 6 strengthens MSC 1 by ... rolling back an interrupted restore, mark the correction explicitly.' The error message MSC 1 shows the user (lines 692-695) already tells them a safety backup exists -- it just never uses it automatically.
